{"world_model":"W1 (mechanism), after E016.

The setup
- The tip is E016: the E015 recipe (Muon on the conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, 9.5 nominal epochs, about 238 steps, widths 128/384/512, max-autotune CUDA graphs) with the SGD weight decay halved to 0.006.
- It scores 6.580 s and 0.7607, a margin of 0.77 pp over the 0.753 bar.

My miss on E016
- I predicted that halving weight decay would be flat, because Muon ignores it. It gave +0.33 pp over E015 (and +0.6 pp over E010).
- Mechanism: weight decay still acts on the 100-way head and the BN biases. Under label smoothing 0.3 with a 1/9 logit scale, the decay on the head (coupled, scaled by wd/lr) shrinks the logit margins every step. With so few steps, that over-regularizes the classes.
- I count about +0.2 pp of the gain as real and the rest as reshuffle (identical-math changes have moved the mean by ±0.27 pp).
- Lesson: head and BN regularization is a live lever. LR, LS and the floor are not.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time.
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp.
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time.
- Resizing 24/28/32: −19 to −22% time and −0.6 pp. A 20 px stage is a cliff (−1.3 pp), because the group-3 maps drop to 2×2.
- Cutting 0.5 epoch: −0.18 pp and −4.8% time.
- Width 576→512: −0.25 pp and −4.8% time.
- CUDA graphs: −0.9%.
- Weight decay ×0.5: +0.33 pp.
- Flat (within ±0.1 pp): the LR floor, LS 0.2, Muon lr ×1.5.

Time model
- Time is GPU-bound and close to proportional to conv FLOPs: E010 cut FLOPs by 5.6% and time by 4.8%.
- Per-step cost scales with pixel count, plus a fixed cost of about 0.3-0.4 s.
- FLOP split per pixel-pass: group 1 about 18%, group 2 about 49%, group 3 about 33%.
- Time levers:
  - narrowing group 2 to 320: about −16% FLOPs, so about −10 to −13% time;
  - dropping the 28 px phase in favour of 24 px: −8% compute, about −6% time;
  - cutting 0.75 epoch at 24 px: about −5.5%.
- Launch overhead is about 1%. Remaining host syncs might save 1-2%.

Accuracy model
- Endpoint averaging dominates. The alpha ramp 0.95^5·(k/T)^3 makes the EMA track the live weights early and average about 20 steps at the end.
- The Lookahead write-back also damps the fast weights. A plain EMA probably loses only 0.1-0.3 pp.
- Accuracy is mostly set in the final high-resolution, low-LR phase. Early 24 px steps are cheap, low-value steps, though 24 px is the floor (20 px is the cliff).
- Exchange rates for buying time with accuracy:
  - epochs: about 0.37 pp per 10% time;
  - width (group 3): about 0.5 pp per 10%;
  - moderate resizing: about 0.3 pp per 10%.
- Group 2 is the wide feature stage at 8×8 after the pool, so narrowing it probably costs more per FLOP than group 3 did.

Noise
- An unchanged recipe is bit-identical (E012), but a fresh max-autotune cache may reselect kernels.
- Any change to the kernel or RNG path reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. Seed std is about 0.25 pp.
- I treat 0.7607 as a true value of about 0.758-0.759.

Strategy
- With 0.77 pp of margin, spend it on FLOP cuts: drop the 28 px phase, trim 24 px epochs, narrow group 2. Aim to sit at about 0.756.
- Cheap scalar regularization probes (head wd ×0.25, a separate wd for the head) can buy margin.

Unsure
- The held-out seed offset.
- Whether halving wd was mostly reshuffle.
- Whether accuracy really lives in the 32 px phase.

W1 (mechanism), after E016.

The setup
- The tip is E016: the E015 recipe (Muon on the conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, 9.5 nominal epochs, about 238 steps, widths 128/384/512, max-autotune CUDA graphs) with the SGD weight decay halved to 0.006.
- It scores 6.580 s and 0.7607, a margin of 0.77 pp over the 0.753 bar.

My miss on E016
- I predicted that halving weight decay would be flat, because Muon ignores it. It gave +0.33 pp over E015 (and +0.6 pp over E010).
- Mechanism: weight decay still acts on the 100-way head and the BN biases. Under label smoothing 0.3 with a 1/9 logit scale, the decay on the head (coupled, scaled by wd/lr) shrinks the logit margins every step. With so few steps, that over-regularizes the classes.
- I count about +0.2 pp of the gain as real and the rest as reshuffle (identical-math changes have moved the mean by ±0.27 pp).
- Lesson: head and BN regularization is a live lever. LR, LS and the floor are not.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time.
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp.
- Muon: +0.66 pp for +4% time.
- Resizing 24/28/32: −19 to −22% time and −0.6 pp. A 20 px stage is a cliff (−1.3 pp), because the group-3 maps drop to 2×2.
- Cutting 0.5 epoch: −0.18 pp and −4.8% time.
- Width 576→512: −0.25 pp and −4.8% time.
- CUDA graphs: −0.9%.
- Weight decay ×0.5: +0.33 pp.
- Flat (within ±0.1 pp): the LR floor, LS 0.2, Muon lr ×1.5.

Time model
- Time is GPU-bound and close to proportional to conv FLOPs: E010 cut FLOPs by 5.6% and time by 4.8%.
- Per-step cost scales with pixel count, plus a fixed cost of about 0.3-0.4 s.
- FLOP split per pixel-pass: group 1 about 18%, group 2 about 49%, group 3 about 33%.
- Time levers:
  - narrowing group 2 to 320: about −16% FLOPs, so about −10 to −13% time;
  - dropping the 28 px phase in favour of 24 px: −8% compute, about −6% time;
  - cutting 0.75 epoch at 24 px: about −5.5%.
- Launch overhead is about 1%. Remaining host syncs might save 1-2%.

Accuracy model
- Endpoint averaging dominates. The alpha ramp 0.95^5·(k/T)^3 makes the EMA track the live weights early and average about 20 steps at the end.
- The Lookahead write-back also damps the fast weights. A plain EMA probably loses only 0.1-0.3 pp.
- Accuracy is mostly set in the final high-resolution, low-LR phase. Early 24 px steps are cheap, low-value steps, though 24 px is the floor (20 px is the cliff).
- Exchange rates for buying time with accuracy:
  - epochs: about 0.37 pp per 10% time;
  - width (group 3): about 0.5 pp per 10%;
  - moderate resizing: about 0.3 pp per 10%.
- Group 2 is the wide feature stage at 8×8 after the pool, so narrowing it probably costs more per FLOP than group 3 did.

Noise
- An unchanged recipe is bit-identical (E012), but a fresh max-autotune cache may reselect kernels.
- Any change to the kernel or RNG path reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. Seed std is about 0.25 pp.
- I treat 0.7607 as a true value of about 0.758-0.759.

Strategy
- With 0.77 pp of margin, spend it on FLOP cuts: drop the 28 px phase, trim 24 px epochs, narrow group 2. Aim to sit at about 0.756.
- Cheap scalar regularization probes (head wd ×0.25, a separate wd for the head) can buy margin.

Unsure
- The held-out seed offset.
- Whether halving wd was mostly reshuffle.
- Whether accuracy really lives in the 32 px phase.
- Group-2 width sensitivity on CIFAR-100.

forecasts.reason: Endpoint averaging over about 20 steps carries most of the gain. Without write-back the fast weights get noisier, costing about 0.2 pp, which is within the 0.3 pp the hypothesis allows; time is unchanged.
Average pixels per step fall by 8% (773 to 710), so time drops about 6%. The 32 px tail is untouched and 24 px stays above the cliff, so the loss is about 0.4 pp and the run likely stays feasible.
About 19 fewer 24 px steps at roughly 19 ms each saves about 0.36 s. Stretching the schedules makes the cost a smooth −0.2 to −0.3 pp, in line with the E008 slope.
A fresh max-autotune cache may pick different kernels through timing noise, so bit-identical results are roughly a coin flip. The held-out mean is probably 0.2-0.3 pp below 0.7607.
Orthogonalization normalizes the step size, so higher momentum only changes how directions are smoothed. Muon scalars have been flat, so a gain of 0.3 pp or more is unlikely.

About −16% conv FLOPs (time has tracked FLOPs closely) gives roughly −9% time. Group 2 is the main feature stage, so expect −0.5 to −0.9 pp, borderline against the bar. The width cut does not really test H1.5's accuracy-per-epoch claim.

cruxes: What is the held-out (seeds 3-12) mean of the E016 tip relative to 0.7607? It decides how much of the 0.77 pp margin can safely go on FLOP cuts.
Is accuracy set mainly in the 32 px low-LR tail? If so, the 28 px phase and early 24 px epochs can be cut almost for free (I023/I024).
Was E016's +0.33 pp from halving weight decay a real head/BN regularization effect or a kernel reshuffle? If real, a further head-wd cut buys margin that can go on narrowing group 2.
